chief_complaint: numbness in feet, trouble walking, and fatigue
hpi_details: 60M presents with progressive tingling and numbness in both feet, causing him to stumble. He also reports severe fatigue, a sore tongue, and mild memory issues. He had a partial gastrectomy 5 years ago for an ulcer.

core_concepts: B12 deficiency causes macrocytic anemia and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord (neuropathy, ataxia).
Gastrectomy eliminates intrinsic factor, causing failure of B12 absorption.
common_misconceptions: Giving folate alone, which corrects the anemia but allows irreversible neurological damage to progress.
dangerous_errors: Missing the neurological signs of B12 deficiency.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: UpToDate & National Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines 2026

reference_soap.subjective: 60M with neuropathy, ataxia, glossitis, and history of partial gastrectomy.
reference_soap.objective: Decreased vibratory and position sense in lower extremities. Positive Romberg. Beefy red, smooth tongue.
reference_soap.assessment: Vitamin B12 deficiency (Macrocytic Anemia and neuropathy).
reference_soap.plan: CBC, peripheral smear, Vitamin B12 and folate levels. Start IM Vitamin B12 injections.

learning_objectives: Recognize the neurological complications and causes of Vitamin B12 deficiency.

teaching.one_liner: Progressive neuropathy, ataxia, and fatigue in a patient with a history of gastrectomy, suggestive of Vitamin B12 deficiency.

must_ask.say: When did the numbness in your feet and the trouble walking start?
Have you ever had stomach surgery, or do you follow a strict vegan diet?
Have you noticed a sore or smooth-feeling tongue, or any changes in your appetite?
Have you noticed any problems with your balance or coordination, especially in the dark?
How is the fatigue affecting your ability to do your usual daily activities?

history.answer: My feet have been tingling and numb, and lately I've been stumbling and having a hard time walking normally.
It is mostly numbness, tingling, and feeling like I am walking on pins and needles, but my muscles don't feel paralyzed or weak.
It started in both feet at the same time and has slowly worked its way up past my ankles symmetrically. My hands just started feeling slightly tingly too.
It started very gradually about four or five months ago, not suddenly, and it has been steadily progressing.
It is definitely getting worse over time; the numbness is spreading higher up my calves, and I stumble more frequently.
I stumble when walking, especially in the dark or when I close my eyes in the shower, but I can still button my shirt and hold cups.
Walking in dim light makes my balance much worse, but movement or resting doesn't change the tingling itself.
No, I have no neck pain, lower back pain, or shooting pains down my legs.
No slurred speech, no facial drooping, no double vision, and no sudden dizziness.
No, I have normal bladder and bowel control, and no numbness around my groin or buttocks.
No shortness of breath, no trouble chewing or swallowing, and my eyelids never droop.
No, I haven't noticed any muscle twitches, cramps, or shrinkage in my arms or legs.
No fever, no chills, and no diarrhea or respiratory infections before this started.
I don't have high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or heart rhythm problems, and I have never smoked.
I had a partial gastrectomy five years ago for a bleeding stomach ulcer, and I take omeprazole regularly. I eat a regular diet with meat and fish.
My tongue has felt burning and sore for the past month, and foods sometimes sting it. I haven't had any nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain.
I feel utterly exhausted and drained every single day, even after a full night of sleep, which started around the same time as the tingling.
I've noticed I'm a bit forgetful lately and misplace things more often, which is frustrating.
I only take omeprazole 20 mg once a day for acid reflux. I don't take diuretics, steroids, chemotherapy, or vitamin supplements.
I am worried because I read this might be a nerve disease like peripheral neuropathy.
My biggest fear is that my memory slips and stumbling mean I'm developing dementia or Alzheimer's disease.
I was hoping you could order a nerve conduction test or something to figure out why my nerves are acting up.
Aside from the stomach surgery and acid reflux, I have no chronic illnesses.
Only the partial gastrectomy five years ago; no other surgeries or hospitalizations.
I have no known allergies to any medications or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes in my life.
I drink about one can of beer once or twice a month, nothing heavy.
I work as a desk clerk at a community center and live with my wife. I don't do heavy manual labor or repetitive wrist straining.
No one in my family has had early nerve disorders, blood diseases, or dementia.

exam.finding: Alert, mildly pale appearance, appearing fatigued but in no acute distress.
Blood pressure 125/78 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm regular, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6 C, SpO2 99% on room air.
Mild conjunctival pallor bilaterally; sclerae are anicteric.
Beefy red, smooth, depapillated tongue without oral ulcerations or mucosal bleeding.
Oriented to person, place, and time; scored 27/30 on MMSE with mild deficits in delayed recall.
Cranial nerves II through XII intact, normal extraocular movements, symmetrical facial expression, no dysarthria.
Normal bulk and tone in all four extremities; motor strength is 5/5 throughout without fasciculations or focal weakness.
Significantly decreased vibration and proprioception in both feet and ankles up to mid-shin; light touch and pinprick sensation mildly reduced in a stocking distribution.
Knee jerk reflexes slightly brisk bilaterally, ankle jerks diminished bilaterally; bilateral plantar responses are extensor (Babinski positive).
Positive Romberg test with marked unsteadiness upon eye closure; wide-based, sensory ataxic gait. Normal finger-to-nose testing.
No cervical or lumbar spine tenderness; negative straight leg raise bilaterally; negative Spurling, Tinel, and Phalen signs.
